title: Encode and Decode Strings
description:
Write two methods. `encode` turns a list of strings into a single string, and `decode` turns that single string back into the exact original list. The encoded text may be sent over a network, so your format must survive **any** characters inside the strings (including whatever separator you might pick) and must handle empty strings and an empty list.

The two methods must not rely on shared state; `decode` only receives the string that `encode` produced.
constraints: strs[i] may contain any Unicode characters
hints: A single delimiter character fails when a string contains that character. What information could you add that doesn't depend on the contents?
Put each string's length in front of it. Then you never need to scan inside the string for a boundary.
Encode each string as `length + '#' + string`. When decoding, read digits up to '#', then take exactly that many characters and continue after them.

solution.explanation: Prefix every string with its length and a '#' marker. Because decode reads the number first, it knows exactly how many characters belong to the string, so any characters inside (including '#' and digits) are harmless. Decoding moves a pointer: find the next '#' from the pointer, parse the length, slice that many characters, and jump past them. Both directions touch each character once, so time and space are O(n) in the total length.
